complexity.correctness_reason: A degenerate (fully skewed) tree of more than ~1000 nodes — well within the 100,000-node constraint — exceeds CPython's default recursion limit and raises RecursionError; the same traversal written iteratively with an explicit stack would not have this failure.
complexity.notes: Compact and idiomatic: using a default argument to thread the path maximum and adding the boolean comparison directly are both neat. The `else` after the early `return` is unnecessary. The one real problem is recursion depth — see correctness_reason.
complexity.summary: Recursive DFS that carries the maximum value seen so far on the root-to-node path via a default parameter, counting a node when its value is at least that running maximum. Each node is visited once; the recursion stack is O(h), which is O(n) for a skewed tree.
